For surface anaesthesia cinchocaine has been used, as the base or hydrochloride, in creams and ointments containing up to 1% and in suppositories for the temporary relief of pain and itching asso- ciated with skin and anorectal conditions. Cinchocaine benzoate has also been used topically. Action. For a comparison of the vasoactivity of cinchocaine and some other local anaesthetics, see p.1852. Plasma cholinesterase deficiency. For mention of the use of cinchocaine in the determination of plasma cholinesterase activ- ity, see under Precautions of Suxamethonium Chloride, p.1911.
